translations.literal: By old army law, anyone who harbored a bandit spy had his family slaughtered. Su abolished that law and treated spies generously. Spies in turn reported the enemy's situation to Su, and Su came to know the bandits' strength and weakness all the better.
translations.idiomatic: By old army law, anyone who harbored a bandit spy had his family slaughtered. Su abolished that law and treated spies generously. Spies in turn reported the enemy's situation to Su, and Su came to know the bandits' strength and weakness all the better.

sentences.zh: 陳許節度使李光顏勇冠諸軍，賊悉以精卒抗光顏。

translations.literal: Chenxu military governor Li Guangyan's courage topped all armies. The bandits sent all their elite troops against Guangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxu military governor Li Guangyan's courage topped all armies. The bandits sent all their elite troops against Guangyan.

sentences.zh: 由是愬乘其無備，十月，將襲蔡州。

translations.literal: Su therefore took advantage of their lack of guard. In the tenth month he prepared to raid Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su therefore took advantage of their lack of guard. In the tenth month he prepared to raid Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其月七日，使判官鄭澥告師期於裴度。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of that month he had his aide Zheng Xie report the date of the attack to Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of that month he had his aide Zheng Xie report the date of the attack to Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 十日夜，以李祐率突將三千為先鋒，李忠義副之，愬自帥中軍三千，田進誠以後軍三千殿而行。

translations.literal: On the night of the tenth he sent Li You at the head of three thousand shock troops as vanguard, with Li Zhongyi as second, Su himself leading three thousand in the center army, and Tian Jincheng with three thousand in the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the tenth he sent Li You at the head of three thousand shock troops as vanguard, with Li Zhongyi as second, Su himself leading three thousand in the center army, and Tian Jincheng with three thousand in the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 初出文成柵，眾請所向，愬曰：「東六十里止。」

translations.literal: When they first left the Wencheng stockade the troops asked where they were going. Su said, "Sixty li east and stop."
translations.idiomatic: When they first left the Wencheng stockade the troops asked where they were going. Su said, "Sixty li east and stop."

sentences.zh: 至賊境，曰張柴砦，盡殺其戍卒，令軍士少息，繕羈靮甲胄，發刃彀弓，復建旆而出。

translations.literal: Reaching bandit territory they came to Zhangchai stockade, killed all the garrison troops, let the soldiers rest briefly, repaired bridles and armor, strung bows and fitted arrows, and marched out again under fresh banners.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching bandit territory they came to Zhangchai stockade, killed all the garrison troops, let the soldiers rest briefly, repaired bridles and armor, strung bows and fitted arrows, and marched out again under fresh banners.

sentences.zh: 是日，陰晦雨雪，大風裂旗旆，馬栗而不能躍，士卒苦寒，抱戈僵仆者道路相望。

translations.literal: That day the sky was dark with wind and snow. Gale winds tore the banners. Horses trembled and could not leap. The soldiers suffered bitter cold; men clutching spears and frozen stiff lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky was dark with wind and snow. Gale winds tore the banners. Horses trembled and could not leap. The soldiers suffered bitter cold; men clutching spears and frozen stiff lined the road.

sentences.zh: 其川澤梁逕險夷，張柴已東，師人未嘗蹈其境，皆謂投身不測。

translations.literal: The marshes, rivers, bridges, and paths were treacherous or easy by turns. East of Zhangchai the army had never trod that land. All said they were throwing themselves into the unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The marshes, rivers, bridges, and paths were treacherous or easy by turns. East of Zhangchai the army had never trod that land. All said they were throwing themselves into the unknown.

sentences.zh: 初至張柴，諸將請所止，愬曰：「入蔡州取吳元濟也。」

translations.literal: When they first reached Zhangchai the generals asked where to halt. Su said, "Into Cai Prefecture to take Wu Yuanji."
translations.idiomatic: When they first reached Zhangchai the generals asked where to halt. Su said, "Into Cai Prefecture to take Wu Yuanji."

sentences.zh: 諸將失色。

translations.literal: The generals turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: The generals turned pale.

sentences.zh: 監軍使哭而言曰：「果落李祐計中！」

translations.literal: The army monitor wept and said, "We have indeed fallen into Li You's plan!"
translations.idiomatic: The army monitor wept and said, "We have indeed fallen into Li You's plan!"

sentences.zh: 愬不聽，促令進軍，皆謂必不生還，然已從愬之令，無敢為身計者。

translations.literal: Su would not listen and urged the army forward. All thought they would surely not return alive, yet having already obeyed Su's order, none dared plan for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Su would not listen and urged the army forward. All thought they would surely not return alive, yet having already obeyed Su's order, none dared plan for himself.

sentences.zh: 醖道分五百人斷洄曲路橋，其夜凍死者十二三。

translations.literal: Su sent five hundred men to cut the bridge on the Huaiqu road. That night one or two out of ten froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent five hundred men to cut the bridge on the Huaiqu road. That night one or two out of ten froze to death.

sentences.zh: 又分五百人斷朗山路。

translations.literal: He sent another five hundred men to cut the Langshan road.
translations.idiomatic: He sent another five hundred men to cut the Langshan road.

sentences.zh: 自張柴行七十里，比至懸瓠城，夜半，雪愈甚。

translations.literal: From Zhangchai they marched seventy li. When they reached Xuanshi City it was midnight and the snow grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhangchai they marched seventy li. When they reached Xuanshi City it was midnight and the snow grew heavier.

sentences.zh: 近城有鵝鴨池，愬令驚擊之，以雜其聲。

translations.literal: Near the city was a pool of geese and ducks. Su ordered them startled and beaten so the noise would mix with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Near the city was a pool of geese and ducks. Su ordered them startled and beaten so the noise would mix with the rest.

sentences.zh: 賊恃吳房、朗山之固，晏然無一人知者。

translations.literal: The bandits, trusting in the strength of Wu Fang and Langshan, were at ease. Not one man knew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, trusting in the strength of Wu Fang and Langshan, were at ease. Not one man knew.

sentences.zh: 李祐、李忠義坎墉而先登，敢銳者從之，盡殺守門卒而登其門，留擊柝者。

translations.literal: Li You and Li Zhongyi scaled the wall first. The boldest followed, killed all the gate guards, mounted the gate, and left men to strike the night watch.
translations.idiomatic: Li You and Li Zhongyi scaled the wall first. The boldest followed, killed all the gate guards, mounted the gate, and left men to strike the night watch.

sentences.zh: 黎明，雪亦止，愬入，止元濟外宅。

translations.literal: At dawn the snow also stopped. Su entered and halted at Yuanji's outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the snow also stopped. Su entered and halted at Yuanji's outer residence.

sentences.zh: 蔡吏告元濟曰：「城已陷矣。」

translations.literal: A Cai official told Yuanji, "The city has fallen."
translations.idiomatic: A Cai official told Yuanji, "The city has fallen."

sentences.zh: 元濟曰：「是洄曲子弟歸求寒衣耳。」

translations.literal: Yuanji said, "It is only the Huaiqu boys coming back for winter clothes."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "It is only the Huaiqu boys coming back for winter clothes."

sentences.zh: 俄聞愬軍號令將士云：「常侍傳語。」

translations.literal: Soon they heard Su's army calling orders to the troops: "The Regular Attendant sends word."
translations.idiomatic: Soon they heard Su's army calling orders to the troops: "The Regular Attendant sends word."

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「何常侍得至於此？」

translations.literal: He then said, "How did the Regular Attendant get here?"
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "How did the Regular Attendant get here?"

sentences.zh: 遂驅率左右乘子城拒捍。

translations.literal: He then drove his followers to mount the inner wall and resist.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove his followers to mount the inner wall and resist.

sentences.zh: 田進誠以兵環而攻之。

translations.literal: Tian Jincheng surrounded it with troops and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jincheng surrounded it with troops and attacked.

sentences.zh: 愬計元濟猶望董重質來救，乃令訪重質家安恤之，使其家人持書召重質。

translations.literal: Su judged that Yuanji still hoped Dong Chongzhi would come to save him. He ordered Chongzhi's family sought out and comforted and had his kin carry a letter summoning Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Su judged that Yuanji still hoped Dong Chongzhi would come to save him. He ordered Chongzhi's family sought out and comforted and had his kin carry a letter summoning Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 重質單騎而歸愬，白衣泥首，愬以客禮待之。

translations.literal: Chongzhi rode alone back to Su in plain clothes with mud on his head. Su received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi rode alone back to Su in plain clothes with mud on his head. Su received him with guest ceremony.

sentences.zh: 田進誠焚子城南門，元濟城上請罪，進誠梯而下之，乃檻送京師。

translations.literal: Tian Jincheng burned the south gate of the inner wall. Yuanji asked forgiveness from atop the wall. Jincheng brought him down on a ladder and sent him to the capital in a cage.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jincheng burned the south gate of the inner wall. Yuanji asked forgiveness from atop the wall. Jincheng brought him down on a ladder and sent him to the capital in a cage.

sentences.zh: 其申、光二州及諸鎮兵尚二萬余人，相次來降。

translations.literal: The Shen and Guang prefectures and garrison troops, more than twenty thousand men in all, surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Shen and Guang prefectures and garrison troops, more than twenty thousand men in all, surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 自元濟就擒，愬不戮一人，其為元濟執事帳下廚廄之間者，皆復其職，使之不疑。

translations.literal: From the time Yuanji was captured Su killed no one. Those who had served Yuanji in office, tent, kitchen, and stable were all restored to their posts so they would not doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Yuanji was captured Su killed no one. Those who had served Yuanji in office, tent, kitchen, and stable were all restored to their posts so they would not doubt him.

sentences.zh: 乃屯兵鞠場以待裴度。

translations.literal: He then encamped on the drill ground to await Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: He then encamped on the drill ground to await Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 翌日，度至，愬具櫜鞬候度馬首。

translations.literal: The next day Du arrived. Su presented arms and waited at the head of Du's horse.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Du arrived. Su presented arms and waited at the head of Du's horse.

sentences.zh: 度將避之，愬曰：「此方不識上下等威之分久矣，請公因以示之。」

translations.literal: Du was about to avoid this. Su said, "This region has long not known the difference between high and low in authority. Please let the lord show it through this."
translations.idiomatic: Du was about to avoid this. Su said, "This region has long not known the difference between high and low in authority. Please let the lord show it through this."

sentences.zh: 度以宰相禮受愬迎謁，眾皆聳觀。

translations.literal: Du received Su's welcome with the ceremony due a chief minister, and all looked on in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Du received Su's welcome with the ceremony due a chief minister, and all looked on in awe.

sentences.zh: 明日，愬軍還於文成柵。

translations.literal: The next day Su's army returned to the Wencheng stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Su's army returned to the Wencheng stockade.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔以愬檢校尚書左僕射，兼襄州刺史、山南東道節度、襄鄧隨唐復郢均房等州觀察等使、上柱國，封涼國公，食邑三千戶，食實封五百戶，一子五品正員。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict made Su Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as Prefect of Xiang Prefecture, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, observer of Xiang, Deng, Sui, Tang, Fu, Ying, Jun, and Fang, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Liang with an estate of three thousand households and a real fief of five hundred, and one son in regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict made Su Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as Prefect of Xiang Prefecture, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, observer of Xiang, Deng, Sui, Tang, Fu, Ying, Jun, and Fang, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Liang with an estate of three thousand households and a real fief of five hundred, and one son in regular fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 憲宗有意復隴右故地，元和十三年五月，授愬鳳翔隴右節度使，仍詔路由闕下。

translations.literal: Xianzong intended to recover the old Longyou lands. In the fifth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he appointed Su military governor of Fengxiang and Longyou, with orders to pass through the capital on his route.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong intended to recover the old Longyou lands. In the fifth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he appointed Su military governor of Fengxiang and Longyou, with orders to pass through the capital on his route.

sentences.zh: 愬未發，屬李師道再叛，詔田弘正、義成、宣武等軍討之，乃移愬為徐州刺史、武寧軍節度使，代其兄願。

translations.literal: Before Su set out Li Shidao rebelled again. An edict sent Tian Hongzheng and the Yicheng and Xuanwu armies against him. Su was then moved to Prefect of Xu Prefecture and military governor of the Wuning Army, replacing his elder brother Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before Su set out Li Shidao rebelled again. An edict sent Tian Hongzheng and the Yicheng and Xuanwu armies against him. Su was then moved to Prefect of Xu Prefecture and military governor of the Wuning Army, replacing his elder brother Yuan.

sentences.zh: 兄弟交換岐、徐二鎮，旬日間再踐父兄之任。

translations.literal: The brothers exchanged the Qi and Xu commands. Within ten days they twice stepped into their father and elder brother's posts.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers exchanged the Qi and Xu commands. Within ten days they twice stepped into their father and elder brother's posts.

sentences.zh: 愬至徐方，理兵有方略。

translations.literal: When Su reached Xu he governed the army with method.
translations.idiomatic: When Su reached Xu he governed the army with method.

sentences.zh: 時蔡將董重質貶春州司戶，愬上表請恕重質賜之，堪於軍前驅使，即詔征還送武寧軍，愬乃署為牙將。

translations.literal: At the time the Cai general Dong Chongzhi had been demoted to Registrar of Chun Prefecture. Su memorialized asking that Chongzhi be pardoned and granted to him, fit for service at the front. An edict at once recalled him and sent him to the Wuning Army, and Su appointed him a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Cai general Dong Chongzhi had been demoted to Registrar of Chun Prefecture. Su memorialized asking that Chongzhi be pardoned and granted to him, fit for service at the front. An edict at once recalled him and sent him to the Wuning Army, and Su appointed him a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 愬破賊金鄉，凡十一戰，擒賊將五十，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: Su defeated the bandits at Jinxiang in eleven battles, captured fifty bandit generals, and killed or captured more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Su defeated the bandits at Jinxiang in eleven battles, captured fifty bandit generals, and killed or captured more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 淄青平，將有事燕、趙。

translations.literal: When Ziqing was pacified there were plans for action in Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziqing was pacified there were plans for action in Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年九月，以愬檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事、潞州大都督府長史、昭義節度使，仍賜興寧裏第。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe Su was made Acting Left Vice Director, Co-Equal with the Secretariat, Chief Ministerial Prefect of Lu Prefecture, and military governor of Zhaoyi, and was granted a residence in Xingning Ward.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe Su was made Acting Left Vice Director, Co-Equal with the Secretariat, Chief Ministerial Prefect of Lu Prefecture, and military governor of Zhaoyi, and was granted a residence in Xingning Ward.

sentences.zh: 十月，王承宗卒，魏博田弘正移任鎮州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Wang Chengzong died. Tian Hongzheng of Weibo was transferred to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wang Chengzong died. Tian Hongzheng of Weibo was transferred to Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 愬至潞州，四月，遷魏州大都督府長史、魏博節度使。

translations.literal: When Su reached Lu Prefecture, in the fourth month he was moved to Chief Ministerial Prefect of Wei Prefecture and military governor of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: When Su reached Lu Prefecture, in the fourth month he was moved to Chief Ministerial Prefect of Wei Prefecture and military governor of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，幽、鎮復亂，愬聞之，素服以令三軍曰：「魏人所以富庶而能通知聖化者，由田公故也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing You and Zhen rebelled again. When Su heard it he put on plain clothes and ordered the whole army, saying, "The reason the people of Wei are rich and can receive the sage's transforming influence is because of Lord Tian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing You and Zhen rebelled again. When Su heard it he put on plain clothes and ordered the whole army, saying, "The reason the people of Wei are rich and can receive the sage's transforming influence is because of Lord Tian.

sentences.zh: 天子以其仁而愛人，使理鎮、冀。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because he is humane and loves men, sent him to govern Zhen and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven, because he is humane and loves men, sent him to govern Zhen and Ji.

sentences.zh: 且田公出於魏，撫師七年，一旦鎮人不道，敢茲殘害，以魏為無人也。

translations.literal: Moreover Lord Tian came from Wei and led the army seven years. In one morning the men of Zhen were wicked and dared such slaughter, as though Wei had no men.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Lord Tian came from Wei and led the army seven years. In one morning the men of Zhen were wicked and dared such slaughter, as though Wei had no men.

sentences.zh: 若父兄子弟食田公恩者，其何以報？」

translations.literal: If fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers who ate Lord Tian's grace—how can they repay it?"
translations.idiomatic: If fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers who ate Lord Tian's grace—how can they repay it?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆慟哭。

translations.literal: The crowd all wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd all wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 又以玉帶、寶劍與牛元翼，遣使謂之曰：「吾先人常以此劍立大勛，吾又以此劍平蔡寇，今鎮人叛逆，公以此翦之。」

translations.literal: He also gave Niu Yuanji a jade belt and precious sword and sent a messenger saying to him, "My forebear once established great merit with this sword. I too pacified the Cai bandits with it. Now the men of Zhen rebel. Use this to cut them down."
translations.idiomatic: He also gave Niu Yuanji a jade belt and precious sword and sent a messenger saying to him, "My forebear once established great merit with this sword. I too pacified the Cai bandits with it. Now the men of Zhen rebel. Use this to cut them down."

sentences.zh: 元翼承命感激，乃以劍及帶令於軍中，報之曰：「願以眾從，竭其死力」。

translations.literal: Yuanji received the order with gratitude and had the sword and belt displayed in the army, replying, "I wish to follow with my force and spend my life to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji received the order with gratitude and had the sword and belt displayed in the army, replying, "I wish to follow with my force and spend my life to the end."

sentences.zh: 方有制置，會疾作，不能治軍，人違紀律，功遂無成。

translations.literal: Just as arrangements were being made illness seized him. He could not govern the army. Men broke discipline, and the enterprise came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Just as arrangements were being made illness seized him. He could not govern the army. Men broke discipline, and the enterprise came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以田布代之，除太子少保，歸東都。

translations.literal: The court replaced him with Tian Bu, made him Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and sent him back to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced him with Tian Bu, made him Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and sent him back to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，卒於洛陽，時年四十九。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month he died in Luoyang at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the tenth month he died in Luoyang at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 穆宗聞之震悼，赗賻加等，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Muzong heard and was shaken with grief. Funeral gifts were raised a grade and he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong heard and was shaken with grief. Funeral gifts were raised a grade and he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 始，晟克復京城，市不改肆；

translations.literal: At first, when Sheng recovered the capital, the markets did not change their stalls;
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Sheng recovered the capital, the markets did not change their stalls;

sentences.zh: 及愬平淮蔡，復踵其美。

translations.literal: when Su pacified Huai and Cai he followed in that excellence.
translations.idiomatic: when Su pacified Huai and Cai he followed in that excellence.

sentences.zh: 父子仍建大勛，雖昆仲皆領兵符，而功業不侔於愬，近代無以比倫。

translations.literal: Father and son both built great merit. Though the brothers all held military seals, none matched Su in achievement. In recent times there has been no comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both built great merit. Though the brothers all held military seals, none matched Su in achievement. In recent times there has been no comparison.

sentences.zh: 加以行己有常，儉不違禮，弟兄席父勛寵，率以仆馬第宅相矜，唯愬六遷大鎮，所處先人舊宅一院而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, his conduct was constant; in frugality he did not violate ritual. His brothers, relying on their father's honors and favor, all boasted of servants, horses, and mansions, while only Su, through six promotions to great commanderies, occupied but one courtyard of their forefather's old residence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his conduct was steady and his frugality never breached propriety. His brothers, resting on their father's honors, mostly vied in servants, horses, and grand houses; only Su, across six promotions to major commands, kept no more than a single courtyard of the family's old home.

sentences.zh: 晚歲忽於取士，辟請不得其人，至使吏緣為奸，軍政不肅，物論稍減，惜哉！

translations.literal: In his later years he suddenly relaxed in recruiting men; his invitations and appointments did not secure the right people, so that clerks used the openings for corruption, military discipline grew slack, and public opinion of him diminished somewhat — a pity!
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew careless about recruiting talent, and the men he summoned were not the right ones. Clerks turned the openings to corruption, military discipline slackened, and his reputation suffered — a pity.

sentences.zh: 聽七歲以廕授太常寺協律郎，常入公署，吏胥小之，不為致敬，聽令鞭之見血，父晟奇之。

translations.literal: Ting at age seven received the post of Coordinating Music Master in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices by hereditary privilege. He often entered the government office; petty clerks looked down on him and would not show respect. Ting ordered them flogged until the blood flowed. His father Sheng marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, Ting received the hereditary post of Coordinating Music Master in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He often came to the government offices; petty clerks slighted him and would not bow. Ting had them whipped until the blood ran. His father Sheng was astonished.

sentences.zh: 後隨吐突承璀討王承宗，為神策行營兵馬使。

translations.literal: Later he followed Tutu Chenghui in the campaign against Wang Chengzong, serving as Military Horse Commissioner of the Divine Strategy Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Tutu Chenghui against Wang Chengzong as Military Horse Commissioner of the Divine Strategy campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時昭義盧從史持兩端，無心討賊，承璀用聽計，擒從史以獻。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi wavered between two sides and had no heart to suppress the rebels; Chenghui used Ting's plan to seize Congshi and present him as captive.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi was hedging and had no will to fight the rebels. Chenghui adopted Ting's plan, seized Congshi, and presented him to the court.

sentences.zh: 轉左驍衛將軍、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Majestic Guard and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Left Majestic Guard with concurrent appointment as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 出為安州刺史，隨鄂嶽觀察使柳公綽討吳元濟，軍中動靜，悉用聽謀，軍聲遂振。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of An Prefecture. Following Observation Commissioner Liu Gongchuo of E-Yue in the campaign against Wu Yuanji, every move in the army used Ting's counsel, and the army's renown flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Prefect of An Prefecture, he joined Observation Commissioner Liu Gongchuo of E-Yue against Wu Yuanji. Every movement in the army followed Ting's counsel, and the army's reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 元和中，討李師道，聽為楚州刺史，統淮南之師。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, in the campaign against Li Shidao, Ting served as Prefect of Chu Prefecture, commanding the Huainan forces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era campaign against Li Shidao, Ting served as Prefect of Chu Prefecture, commanding the Huainan army.

sentences.zh: 鄆人素易淮軍，聽潛訓練，出其不意，趨海州，據險要，破沐陽兵，降朐山戍，懷仁、東海兩城望風乞降，山東平。

translations.literal: The men of Yan had always looked down on the Huainan army. Ting secretly trained his troops, struck where they did not expect, rushed to Haizhou, seized strategic points, defeated the forces at Muyang, reduced the garrison at Qushan, and the two cities of Huairen and Donghai surrendered at the mere rumor of his approach — Shandong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Yan had long despised the Huainan troops. Ting drilled his men in secret, struck by surprise, raced to Haizhou, seized the key positions, routed the Muyang garrison, took Qushan, and Huairen and Donghai surrendered at the news — Shandong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年五月，以功授檢校左散騎常侍、夏州刺史、夏綏銀宥節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, for his merit he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant, Prefect of Xia Prefecture, and Military Governor of Xia-Sui-Yin-You.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yuanhe 14, he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant, Prefect of Xia Prefecture, and Military Governor of Xia-Sui-Yin-You for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，改靈州大都督府長史、靈鹽節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, he was changed to Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture Grand Protectorate and Military Governor of Ling-Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year, he was reassigned as Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture and Military Governor of Ling-Yan.

sentences.zh: 境內有光祿渠，廢塞歲久，欲起屯田以代轉輸，聽復開決舊渠，溉田千余頃，至今賴之。

translations.literal: Within the territory was the Guanglu Canal, long abandoned and blocked. Wishing to establish military colonies to replace transport levies, Ting reopened and cleared the old canal, irrigating more than a thousand qing of fields — people still rely on it today.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanglu Canal within his territory had been blocked for years. Seeking to replace grain transport with military colonies, Ting reopened the old channel and irrigated more than a thousand qing of land — the region still depends on it.

sentences.zh: 就加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon additionally appointed Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，聽為羽林將軍，有名馬，穆宗在東宮，令近侍諷聽獻之，聽以職總親軍，不敢從。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ting was General of the Feathered Forest Guard, he had a famous horse. Muzong, while still in the Eastern Palace, had his close attendants hint that Ting should present it. Ting, holding command over the imperial guard corps, dared not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting was General of the Feathered Forest Guard, he owned a celebrated horse. Muzong, still heir apparent, had attendants suggest that Ting offer it up. Ting, commanding the imperial guard, refused.

sentences.zh: 及即位之始，幽、冀不廷，太原與二鎮接境，方議易帥，宰臣進擬，上皆不允，謂宰臣曰：「李聽為羽林將軍，不與朕馬，是必可任。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of his enthronement, You and Ji refused court obedience. Taiyuan bordered both commanderies, and they were just discussing changing commanders. The chief ministers submitted nominations, but the emperor approved none. He told the chief ministers, "Li Ting, as General of the Feathered Forest Guard, would not give me his horse — he is surely fit for appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign, You and Ji defied the court. Taiyuan bordered both regions, and the court was choosing a new commander. The chief ministers proposed candidates, but the emperor rejected them all. He told his ministers, "Li Ting would not give me his horse when he was Feathered Forest general — that man can be trusted."

sentences.zh: 長慶二年二月，授檢校兵部尚書、太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使，代裴度。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Changqing, he was appointed Acting Minister of War, Magistrate of Taiyuan, Defender of the Northern Capital, and Hedong Military Governor, replacing Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Changqing 2, he was made Acting Minister of War, Magistrate of Taiyuan, Defender of the Northern Capital, and Hedong Military Governor, replacing Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，轉滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, he was transferred to Prefect of Hua Prefecture and Military Governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year, he was transferred to Prefect of Hua Prefecture and Military Governor of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 大和二年，討李同捷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dahe, he campaigned against Li Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 2, he campaigned against Li Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 時魏博行營將丌誌沼潛結滄、鎮，擅回戈攻其帥史憲誠。

translations.literal: At the time the Weibo campaign general Qi Zhizhao secretly colluded with Cang and Zhen, turned his troops without authorization, and attacked his commander Shi Xianjing.
translations.idiomatic: The Weibo campaign general Qi Zhizhao secretly aligned with Cang and Zhen, turned his troops without orders, and attacked his own commander Shi Xianjing.

sentences.zh: 詔聽帥師援之，大破其叛卒，誌沼奔鎮州，為王庭湊所殺，聽遂凱旋，以功封涼國公，授一子五品官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ting to lead troops to his relief. He greatly defeated the mutineers. Zhizhao fled to Zhen Prefecture and was killed by Wang Tingcou. Ting then returned in triumph; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang and one son was granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ting to march to his relief. He crushed the mutineers. Zhizhao fled to Zhen Prefecture and was killed by Wang Tingcou. Ting returned in triumph, was enfeoffed Duke of Liang, and one son received a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 王庭湊再違朝旨，詔聽以全師屯貝州。

translations.literal: Wang Tingcou again defied court orders. An edict ordered Ting to quarter his full army at Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tingcou again defied the court, an edict ordered Ting to camp his full army at Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 路由魏州，史憲誠懼聽見襲，衷甲郊迎，候吏密白呼，乃令兵士匣刃櫜弓，休於野外，魏人遂安。

translations.literal: His route passed through Wei Prefecture. Shi Xianjing feared Ting would attack on sight and came to meet him outside the walls wearing armor beneath his robes. A waiting clerk secretly reported this to Ting, who then ordered his soldiers to sheath their blades and case their bows and rest in the open countryside — the people of Wei were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Wei Prefecture, Shi Xianjing feared an attack and met him outside the walls in hidden armor. A clerk secretly warned Ting, who ordered his men to sheath swords, case bows, and camp in the open — the people of Wei were reassured.

sentences.zh: 後憲誠欲入覲，竭其府庫，魏人怨之，殺憲誠，衙軍立其大將何進滔。

translations.literal: Later Xianjing wished to go to court for audience and emptied his treasury. The people of Wei resented this and killed Xianjing; the garrison guard installed his Grand General He Jintao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xianjing prepared to go to court and drained the treasury. The people of Wei, resentful, killed him; the garrison installed his grand general He Jintao.

sentences.zh: 詔聽兼領魏博節度使，將兵北渡，魏人不納聽，乘城拒守，乃屯兵館陶。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ting to concurrently hold the Weibo command. He led troops north across the river, but the people of Wei would not admit Ting; they manned the walls in defense, so he encamped at Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was ordered to take the Weibo command as well. He led troops north across the river, but Wei would not admit him; they manned the walls, and he encamped at Guantao.

sentences.zh: 魏兵遽襲，聽不為備，其軍大敗，無復部伍，晝夜奔走，僅而獲免，喪師過半，輜車兵仗並皆委棄。

translations.literal: Wei troops suddenly attacked. Ting was unprepared; his army was heavily defeated and lost all formation. Day and night they fled, barely escaping with their lives. More than half the army was lost, and transport wagons and weapons were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops struck without warning. Unprepared, Ting's army was shattered and lost all order. They fled day and night, barely escaping alive. More than half the force was lost, with wagons and arms abandoned.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞溫造、殿中侍御史崔蠡彈之曰：

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao and Palace Attendant Censor Cui Li impeached him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao and Palace Attendant Censor Cui Li impeached him:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞賞罰不立，無以示天下；

translations.literal: "We have heard that when rewards and punishments are not established, there is no way to show the world;
translations.idiomatic: "We have heard that when reward and punishment are not fixed, there is no way to govern the realm;

sentences.zh: 是非一貫，莫能建大中。

translations.literal: when right and wrong do not run consistently, the great balance cannot be upheld.
translations.idiomatic: when right and wrong are not applied consistently, the great order cannot be upheld.

sentences.zh: 竊見義成軍節度使李聽，昨者資其承藉，委以統戎，俾代憲誠，付之雄鎮。

translations.literal: We observe that Military Governor Li Ting of the Yicheng Army, relying on his family standing, was entrusted with command of troops, made to replace Xianjing, and given a mighty commandery.
translations.idiomatic: We observe that Li Ting of the Yicheng Army, relying on family standing, was entrusted with troops, set to replace Xianjing, and given a great command.

sentences.zh: 總二萬虎貔之旅，位極寵榮；

translations.literal: He commanded twenty thousand tiger-and-bear troops and stood at the very height of imperial favor;
translations.idiomatic: He commanded twenty thousand crack troops and stood at the summit of imperial favor;

sentences.zh: 兼兩籓節制之權，心無報效。

translations.literal: he held authority over two circuits, yet his heart showed no repayment of service.
translations.idiomatic: he held two circuits' authority, yet his heart showed no repayment.

sentences.zh: 況陛下授以神算，假以天威，入魏之期，克日先定。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty granted him divine strategy and lent him heavenly authority; the day of entry into Wei was fixed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty gave him divine strategy and lent him imperial authority; the day of entering Wei was set in advance.

sentences.zh: 而聽擁旄觀望，按甲遷延，熒惑人心，逗撓軍政。

translations.literal: Yet Ting, banner in hand, looked on and waited, holding his armor in delay, sowing confusion in men's hearts and frustrating military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ting, banner in hand, looked on and waited, holding his armor in delay, sowing confusion and frustrating the campaign.

sentences.zh: 遂使憲誠陷於屠戮，亂眾肆其奸兇，失六郡於垂成，固危巢於已覆。

translations.literal: Thus Xianjing fell to slaughter, the rebellious masses unleashed their treachery and violence, six prefectures were lost when victory was near at hand, and a dangerous nest was secured even as the old one had already collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xianjing was slaughtered, rebels ran wild, six prefectures were lost on the verge of success, and a new danger was entrenched where the old had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 委貝州而不守，燒劫無遺；

translations.literal: He abandoned Bei Prefecture without defending it, leaving nothing untouched by fire and plunder;
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned Bei Prefecture undefended, leaving nothing unburned or unplundered;

sentences.zh: 望淺口而疾驅，狼狽就道。

translations.literal: he gazed toward Qian Pass and spurred away in haste, fleeing the road in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: he looked toward Qian Pass and fled headlong, leaving in disarray.

sentences.zh: 自圖茍免，不吝苞羞，蔑棄朝章，有同兒戲。

translations.literal: seeking only his own escape, he spared no disgrace, trampled court regulations as if they were child's play.
translations.idiomatic: seeking only to save himself, he spared no shame and treated court law as child's play.

sentences.zh: 魏州之亂，職聽之由，論其負恩，萬死猶幸。

translations.literal: The turmoil in Weizhou arose from Ting's office; considering his betrayal of favor, even ten thousand deaths would still be lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's turmoil arose from Ting's conduct; for such betrayal of favor, even death ten thousand times would be mercy.

sentences.zh: 伏以封常清河南失律，斬於關門；

translations.literal: We submit that Feng Changqing, for losing discipline in Henan, was beheaded at the pass gate;
translations.idiomatic: We submit: Feng Changqing, for losing discipline in Henan, was beheaded at the pass;

sentences.zh: 高霞寓唐鄧破傷，投諸遐裔；

translations.literal: Gao Xiayu, defeated and wounded at Tang and Deng, was cast to distant regions;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiayu, defeated at Tang and Deng, was banished to the frontier;

sentences.zh: 渾鎬節制易定，將戰而兵力不支；

translations.literal: Hun Gao, commanding Yi and Ding, was about to give battle when his forces could not sustain the fight;
translations.idiomatic: Hun Gao, commanding Yi and Ding, was about to fight when his strength failed;

sentences.zh: 袁滋逗留西川，欲進而兇渠尚在。

translations.literal: Yuan Zi lingered in Xichuan, wishing to advance while the rebel chieftain still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi lingered in Xichuan, wishing to advance while the rebel chief still lived.

sentences.zh: 或親當矢石，或躬歷艱危，勢屈賊鋒，竟申朝典，未曾貸法，必震皇威。

translations.literal: Some faced arrows and stones personally, others bore hardship and peril themselves; though overcome by the enemy's edge, the court's laws were carried out in the end. The law was never relaxed — imperial majesty was surely upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Some faced arrows in person, others braved peril themselves; though beaten by the enemy, the court's law was enforced. The law was never waived — imperial majesty was upheld.

sentences.zh: 今李聽罪狀夙聞，中外憤惋，比之常清等輩，萬萬過之。

translations.literal: Now Li Ting's offenses have long been known; court and country alike burn with indignation. Compared with Feng Changqing and those like him, he far exceeds them ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting's crimes have long been known; court and country alike are outraged. Compared with Feng Changqing and his like, he exceeds them ten thousandfold.

sentences.zh: 若陛下猶示含弘，不置極法，臣等恐憲章墜地，天下寒心。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty still shows tolerance and does not apply the extreme law, we fear the statutes will fall to earth and all the world will grow cold at heart.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty still shows mercy and withholds the severest penalty, we fear the law will collapse and the realm will lose heart.

sentences.zh: 伏請付法。」

translations.literal: We respectfully ask that he be handed over to the law."
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully ask that he be handed over to the law."

sentences.zh: 上不之罪，罷兵柄，為太子少師。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish him. His military authority was removed and he was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish him. He was stripped of military command and made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 聽頗賂遺權幸以為援，居無何，復檢校司徒，起為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: Ting gave lavish gifts to powerful favorites to gain support. Before long he was again made Acting Grand Master of the Palace and recalled as Military Governor of Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Ting lavished gifts on powerful favorites for support. Before long he was again made Acting Grand Master of the Palace and recalled as Military Governor of Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 邠州衙廳，相傳不利葺修，以至隳環，聽曰：「帥臣鑿兇門而出，豈有拘於巫祝而隳公署耶！」

translations.literal: The commandery hall at Bin Prefecture was traditionally said to suffer ill fortune if repaired, so it had fallen into ruin. Ting said, "A commander breaks through the Gate of Ill Omen to go forth — how could he be bound by shamans and diviners and let the public offices crumble!"
translations.idiomatic: Bin Prefecture's commandery hall was said to bring ill luck if repaired, and had fallen to ruin. Ting said, "A commander breaks through the Gate of Ill Omen to march forth — how can he be bound by shamans and let public offices crumble!"

sentences.zh: 遂命葺之，卒無變異。

translations.literal: He then ordered it repaired, and in the end nothing untoward occurred.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it repaired, and nothing untoward occurred.

sentences.zh: 大和六年，轉武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dahe, he was transferred to Military Governor of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 6, he was transferred to Military Governor of the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 時聽有蒼頭為徐州將，不欲聽至，聽先使親吏慰勞徐人，為蒼頭所殺。

translations.literal: At the time Ting had a household slave serving as a commander at Xuzhou who did not want Ting to arrive. Ting first sent a trusted clerk to console and reward the people of Xu, but the slave had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: A household slave of Ting's served as a Xuzhou commander and did not want him to come. Ting first sent a trusted clerk to console the people of Xu, but the slave had him killed.

sentences.zh: 聽不敢進，固以疾辭，用為太子太保。

translations.literal: Ting dared not advance and firmly resigned on grounds of illness; he was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Ting dared not advance and firmly resigned on grounds of illness; he was made Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，出守鳳翔，時人榮之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he went out to guard Fengxiang — people of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went out to guard Fengxiang — an appointment people of the time regarded as an honor.

sentences.zh: 九年，改陳許節度，未至鎮，復除太子太保分司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was changed to the Chen-Xu command, but before reaching his post he was again appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent with nominal duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reassigned to the Chen-Xu command, but before reaching his post was again made Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent in nominal service.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，出為河中尹、河中晉慈隰節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, he went out as Magistrate of Hezhong and Military Governor of Hezhong-Jin-Ci-Li.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 1, he went out as Magistrate of Hezhong and Military Governor of Hezhong-Jin-Ci-Li.

sentences.zh: 四年，以疾求代，除太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he requested replacement on grounds of illness and was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked to be relieved on grounds of illness and was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月卒，時年六十一，贈司徒。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month he died, aged sixty-one; he was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He died that tenth month at sixty-one and was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 聽十領節旌，所不至者三鎮。

translations.literal: Ting held the commander's banner ten times; only three commanderies he did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Ting held military governorship ten times; only three commands he never reached.

sentences.zh: 蒞官苛細，好將迎遺賂，故急於聚斂，窮極侈欲。

translations.literal: In office he was harshly meticulous, fond of grand welcomes and accepting gifts, and therefore eager to gather wealth, exhausting resources to satisfy extravagant desires.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was exacting and severe, fond of grand welcomes and gifts, and therefore eager to amass wealth to the limit of extravagance.

sentences.zh: 位至一品，竟終牖下，非西平之遺德，焉能及此乎！

translations.literal: He rose to the first rank yet ended his days beneath his own window — had it not been for the legacy of the Western Pacifier, how could he have reached so high!
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the first rank yet died at home in peace — without the Western Pacifier's legacy, how could he have risen so high!

sentences.zh: 憲，晟第五子。

translations.literal: Xian was Sheng's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was Sheng's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 晟十子，憲、愬最仁孝。

translations.literal: Of Sheng's ten sons, Xian and Su were the most benevolent and filial.
translations.idiomatic: Of Sheng's ten sons, Xian and Su were the most benevolent and filial.

sentences.zh: 及長，好儒術，以禮法修整，起家太原府參軍、醴泉縣尉。

translations.literal: When grown, Xian loved Confucian learning and kept himself disciplined by rites and law. He began his career as Registrar of Taiyuan Prefecture and Magistrate of Liquan County.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he loved Confucian learning and conducted himself by rites and law. He began as Registrar of Taiyuan Prefecture and Magistrate of Liquan County.

sentences.zh: 於頔鎮襄陽，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Yu Di governed Xiangyang, he recruited Xian as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Di governed Xiangyang, he recruited Xian as an aide.

sentences.zh: 時吳少誠據淮西，獨憚頔之威，當時鹹以憲謀畫致之。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Shaocheng held Huaxi; he alone feared Yu Di's might, and people of the day all attributed this to Xian's planning.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng then held Huaxi and feared only Yu Di's might — contemporaries credited Xian's counsel.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，田弘正以魏博奉朝旨，辟憲為從事，授衛州刺史，遷絳州，所至以理行稱。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe, Tian Hongzheng of Weibo submitted to court orders and recruited Xian as an aide, appointing him Prefect of Wei Prefecture and then transferring him to Jiang Prefecture; everywhere he went he was praised for orderly governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 8, Tian Hongzheng of Weibo submitted to the court and recruited Xian, appointing him Prefect of Wei Prefecture and then transferring him to Jiang; everywhere he served he was praised for good governance.

sentences.zh: 入為宗正少卿，遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: He entered court as Junior Director of the Imperial Clan and was promoted to Director of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Junior Director of the Imperial Clan and was promoted to Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以太和公主降回鶻，命金吾大將軍胡證充送公主使，命憲副之。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Princess Taihe was sent in marriage to the Uyghurs. Grand General of the Golden Guard Hu Zheng was appointed chief envoy to escort the princess, and Xian was ordered as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Princess Taihe was sent to marry the Uyghurs. Grand General Hu Zheng of the Golden Guard was made chief escort envoy, with Xian as deputy.

sentences.zh: 使還，獻《入蕃道里記》，遷檢校左散騎常侍，兼太府卿。

translations.literal: On returning from the mission, he presented the "Record of Routes into the Barbarian Lands" and was promoted to Acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Director of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he presented the Record of Routes into the Barbarian Lands and was promoted to Acting Left Regular Attendant with concurrent appointment as Director of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 出為洪州刺史、江西觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Hong Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Prefect of Hong Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 大行二年，轉嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dahe, he was transferred to Military Governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 2, he was transferred to Military Governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 憲雖勛伐之家，然累歷事任，皆以吏能擢用，所履官秩，政績流聞。

translations.literal: Though Xian came from a family of military achievement, through repeated offices he was always promoted for administrative ability; in every rank he held, his governance was widely acclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Though from a family of martial achievement, Xian rose through repeated offices on administrative merit; his governance was widely praised at every post.

sentences.zh: 性本明恕，尤精律學，屢詳決冤獄，活無罪者數百人。

translations.literal: By nature he was clear-minded and forgiving, especially skilled in penal law. He repeatedly examined and resolved wrongful cases, saving hundreds of innocent men.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-minded and forgiving by nature, he was especially skilled in penal law. He repeatedly reviewed wrongful cases and saved hundreds of innocent men.

sentences.zh: 以能入官，官無敗事，士君子多之。

translations.literal: Entering office through ability, he left no post in failure — gentlemen widely approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted for ability, he left no post in failure — gentlemen widely approved of him.

sentences.zh: 大和三年八月卒，時年五十六。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Dahe he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Dahe 3 at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 憑累歷諸衛大將軍，恕太子洗馬，並以廕授官，累遷至少卿監。

translations.literal: Ping successively held the post of Grand General of various guards; Shu served as Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud — both received offices by hereditary privilege and rose through repeated promotions to Junior Director and Directorate posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ping rose through grand generalships of various guards; Shu served as Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud — both entered by hereditary privilege and rose to junior director and directorate posts.

sentences.zh: 惎累官至右龍武大將軍，沈湎酒色，恣為豪侈，積債至數千萬。

translations.literal: Ji rose to Grand General of the Right Dragon Martial Guard. He drowned himself in wine and women, indulged in extravagant luxury, and accumulated debts reaching tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rose to Grand General of the Right Dragon Martial Guard. He drowned in wine and women, lived in reckless luxury, and ran up debts of tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 其子貸回鶻錢一萬余貫不償，為回鶻所訴，文宗怒，貶惎為定州司法參軍。

translations.literal: His son borrowed more than ten thousand strings of cash from the Uyghurs and did not repay; the Uyghurs sued, and Emperor Wenzong grew angry and demoted Ji to Legal Adjutant of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son borrowed more than ten thousand strings of Uyghur cash and failed to repay. The Uyghurs sued; Wenzong was enraged and demoted Ji to Legal Adjutant of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王佖，晟之甥。

translations.literal: Wang Bi was Sheng's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi was Sheng's nephew.

sentences.zh: 雄武善騎射，自晟河西、河北出師，佖無役不從。

translations.literal: Bold and martial, skilled at riding and archery — from Sheng's campaigns west of the river and north of the river, Bi followed every expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and skilled in riding and archery, Bi followed Sheng on every campaign west and north of the river.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，晟攻賊於光泰門，賊鋒尚勁，佖與兵馬使李演逾苑墻血戰，敗賊前鋒，諸軍方振，論功為神策將。

translations.literal: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Sheng attacked the rebels at Guangtai Gate. The rebel edge was still fierce. Bi and Military Horse Commissioner Li Yan leaped the park wall and fought in blood, defeating the rebel vanguard. Only then did the armies recover their spirit; for merit Bi was made a Divine Strategy general.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhu Ci's rebellion, Sheng attacked at Guangtai Gate while the rebel line was still strong. Bi and Military Horse Commissioner Li Yan scaled the park wall and fought through blood, routing the vanguard. The armies rallied; for merit Bi was made a Divine Strategy general.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃之寇涇原，佖伏卒擊尚結贊，幾獲，由是深為吐蕃所畏。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided Jingyuan, Bi ambushed them and struck Shang Jiezan, nearly capturing him; from this the Tibetans came deeply to fear him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans raided Jingyuan, Bi ambushed and struck Shang Jiezan, nearly capturing him — from then on the Tibetans deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 晟視佖恩寵與願、愬不殊，給與過之。

translations.literal: Sheng regarded Bi's favor and honors as no different from those of Yuan and Su, and his gifts to Bi exceeded even theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng favored Bi no less than Yuan and Su, and gave him even more.

sentences.zh: 晟既為張延賞媒孽罷兵權，亦不用佖為將帥，入為左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: After Sheng was stripped of military authority through Zhang Yanshang's slander, he also did not employ Bi as a commander; Bi entered court as Senior General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yanshang's slander cost Sheng his command, he also ceased employing Bi as a general; Bi entered court as Senior General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 元和中，願、愬醖兄弟在方鎮，佖檢校工部尚書、靈州大都督府長史、朔方靈鹽節度使。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Yuan and Su held commands in the regions as brothers in arms; Bi was made Acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture Grand Protectorate, and Shofang-Ling-Yan Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, while Yuan and Su held regional commands, Bi was made Acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture, and Shofang-Ling-Yan Military Governor.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃欲成烏蘭橋於河壖，先貯材木，朔方節度使每遣人潛載之，委於河流，終莫能成。

translations.literal: Previously the Tibetans wished to complete the Wulan Bridge on the riverbank. They first stored timber and building materials; each Shofang military governor secretly sent men to load them into the river, so the bridge could never be completed.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans had long sought to build the Wulan Bridge on the riverbank and stockpiled timber. Each Shofang governor secretly sent men to dump the materials into the river, and the bridge was never finished.

sentences.zh: 至是，蕃人知佖貪而無謀，先厚遺之，然後併役成橋，仍築月城圍守之。

translations.literal: By this time the Tibetans knew Bi was greedy and without strategy. They first gave him rich gifts, then completed the bridge with combined labor and also built a crescent fortress to garrison and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans, knowing Bi greedy and unwise, bribed him heavily, then finished the bridge and built a crescent fortress to hold it.

sentences.zh: 自是朔方禦寇不暇，邊上至今為恨。

translations.literal: From this Shofang had no leisure for defense against raiders, and the frontier still resents it to this day.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Shofang could not keep pace with frontier defense, and the border still bears the grudge.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年四月卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Changqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Changqing 3.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：西平器偉材雄，人望而畏，出身事主，落落有將帥之風，見義能勇，聽受不疑，忠於事君，長於應變，誠一代之賢將也。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: The Western Pacifier was grand in capacity and heroic in talent; men looked on him with awe. From the start in serving his sovereign he bore the bearing of a commander — swift to courage when justice called, prompt to accept counsel without doubt, loyal in serving his ruler, skilled in adapting to change — truly a worthy general of his age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The Western Pacifier was grand in stature and heroic in talent; men looked on him with awe. From his first service he bore a commander's bearing — bold when justice demanded, swift to heed counsel, loyal to his sovereign, skilled in adaptation — a worthy general of his age.

sentences.zh: 觀恒山之役，立談釋二帥之憾；

translations.literal: Consider the campaign at Heng Mountain: in a standing conversation he released the resentment of two commanders;
translations.idiomatic: At Heng Mountain, a few words standing released two commanders' grievances;

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，號哭赴奉天之危，可不為忠義乎！

translations.literal: in the rebellion of the Jing army, he wept and rushed to save Fengtian in crisis — could this not be called loyal righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: in the Jing army rebellion, he wept and rushed to Fengtian's peril — was this not loyal righteousness!

sentences.zh: 對白華之進軍，知平涼之必詐，沮星變之議，移渭橋之軍，可不為應變乎！

translations.literal: facing Baihua's advance, he knew Pingliang must be a ruse; he blocked counsel based on celestial omens and shifted the army at Wei Bridge — could this not be called adaptability!
translations.idiomatic: facing Baihua's advance, he saw Pingliang must be a feint; he blocked counsel from omens and shifted the army at Wei Bridge — was this not adaptability!

sentences.zh: 解帶結孝忠之心，請婚釋延賞之怨，嫉惡有楚琳之請，懲亂行希鑒之誅，可不為明於決斷乎！

translations.literal: loosening his belt won Zhu Xiaozhong's heart; seeking marriage dissolved Zhang Yanshang's resentment; his hatred of evil rejected Chu Lin's petition; punishing rebellion carried out Xi Jian's execution — could this not be called clarity in decision!
translations.idiomatic: loosening his belt won Zhu Xiaozhong's loyalty; seeking marriage dissolved Zhang Yanshang's grudge; rejecting Chu Lin showed hatred of evil; executing Xi Jian punished rebellion — was this not decisive judgment!

sentences.zh: 而德宗皇帝聽斷不明，無人君之量，俾功臣困讒慝之口，奸人秉衡石之權，丁瓊之言，誠堪太息。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Dezong was unclear in judgment and lacked a ruler's measure, letting meritorious servants be trapped by slanderers' mouths while wicked men held the scales of power — Ding Qiong's words truly merit deep sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Dezong judged poorly and lacked a ruler's breadth, letting worthy servants be trapped by slander while wicked men held power — Ding Qiong's case truly merits a sigh.

sentences.zh: 雖齪齪刻渭橋之石，區區賜煙閣之銘，亦何心哉！

translations.literal: Though he painstakingly carved the stone at Wei Bridge and meagerly bestowed an inscription in the Cloud of Glory Pavilion — what was in his heart!
translations.idiomatic: Though he carved the stone at Wei Bridge and granted an inscription in the Cloud of Glory Pavilion — what was in his heart!

sentences.zh: 作善遺慶，諸子俱才，元和平賊之功，聽、愬居其半。

translations.literal: Doing good leaves blessings; all his sons possessed talent. Of the merit in pacifying rebels in the Yuanhe era, Ting and Su accounted for half.
translations.idiomatic: Good deeds leave blessings; all his sons had talent. Of the Yuanhe era's merit in pacifying rebels, Ting and Su accounted for half.

sentences.zh: 父子昆弟，皆以功名始終，道家所忌之談，李氏以善勝矣。

translations.literal: Father and sons, brothers together — all began and ended in merit and fame. What the Daoist school warns against, the Li family overcame through goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Father, sons, and brothers alike began and ended in merit and fame. What Daoists warn against, the Li family overcame through virtue.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：桓桓太師，義勇天資。

translations.literal: Praise says: Grand and mighty the Grand Mentor — righteous courage was his heaven-given nature.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Grand and mighty the Grand Mentor — righteous courage was his heaven-given gift.

sentences.zh: 運鐘禍亂，力拯顛危。

translations.literal: When fortune struck calamity and chaos, he strove with force to save tottering peril.
translations.idiomatic: When calamity struck, he strove with all his strength to save a tottering realm.

sentences.zh: 愬事章武，誅蔡平齊。

translations.literal: Su served Zhangwu, executed Cai and pacified Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Su served Zhangwu, destroyed Cai, and pacified Qi.

sentences.zh: 淩煙畫圖，父子為宜。

translations.literal: Painted on the Cloud-rising Terrace — father and sons were fit indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Painted on the Cloud-rising Terrace — father and sons were fit indeed.
